title: Completed perfect scalar models under arbitrary pullback
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and put $A_n=R/\pi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:V'\to V$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $T=V,V'$ put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $\underline M_T$ denote the constant sheaf of an $R$-module $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of finite projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], with specified differential, and set $C_T(P)=B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T$. These are regarded as objects of the ambient derived categories of $B_T$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $Lg^*$ be the specified strict reduction-tower derived pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], equivalently completed pullback on these derived-complete objects [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

There are natural isomorphisms
$$C_T(P)\otimes^L_{B_T}(A_n)_T\cong(A_n)_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T,$$
$$Lg^*C_V(P)\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n\bigl((A_n)_{V'}\otimes_{\underline R_{V'}}\underline{P^\bullet}_{V'}\bigr)\cong C_{V'}(P).$$
The latter identifies all derived-limit projections with the ordinary quotient maps on the displayed bounded complex. Its finite reductions are induced by the canonical constant-section coefficient maps and preserve the given scalar differentials; they commute with consecutive quotient transitions. The comparisons are natural in chain maps of bounded finite-projective complexes.

For every integer $j$, with $N^j=H^j(P^\bullet)$, the canonical comparison for the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] is
$$\mathcal H^j(C_T(P))\cong B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{N^j}_T.$$
Ordinary ringed pullback $g^*=g^{-1}(-)\otimes_{g^{-1}B_V}B_{V'}$ along the projection-induced coefficient map, with $g^{-1}$ the pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], of this latter sheaf is canonically $B_{V'}\otimes_{\underline R_{V'}}\underline{N^j}_{V'}$: on balanced tensors the isomorphism sends $b'\otimes(b\otimes n)$ to $b'g^\sharp(b)\otimes n$, with inverse $b'\otimes n\mapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes n)$. Consequently, for any integers $a\le b$, vanishing of $\mathcal H^j(C_V(P))$ for $j\notin[a,b]$ implies the same vanishing for $C_{V'}(P)$. No flatness of $B_{V'}$ over $g^{-1}B_V$ is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5) and Proposition 6.6.11, finite perfect scalar models; Stacks Tag 093M (sites-modules.tex, lemma-completion-flat); agent calculation in returned proof Steps 3 and 5, including the projective-summand inverse limit and balanced-tensor identification.

proof.text: The coefficient ring $R$ is a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $(\pi)$ and finite residue field. In particular it is a PID and is Noetherian. Each $A_n$ is finite, its consecutive quotient map is surjective, and it is killed by a power of $\ell$: write $\ell=u\pi^e$ with $e\ge1$ using the extended absolute value and the DVR factorization, and choose $m$ with $em\ge n$. Since $R$ is a domain and $\pi\ne0$, the complex $[R\xrightarrow{\pi^n}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$ resolves $A_n$ by two finite free modules. Thus $(R,(\pi))$ satisfies the hypotheses of the adic coefficient datum, including perfectness of all its quotients. Use its actual coefficient sheaves, completed limit, projections and strict quotient tower. The identification of finite coefficient sheaves with constant sheaves, supplied by the completed-constant reduction theorem, identifies this limit with the $B_T$ in the statement and respects every projection.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), with the finite-coefficient identification of the adic datum; the DVR consequences and its two-term quotient resolution

proof.text:
For each degree $r$, choose a finite set of generators of $P^r$, giving a surjection $s_r:R^{m_r}\to P^r$. Projectivity lifts $1_{P^r}$ through $s_r$ to $i_r$, so $s_ri_r=1$. Applying constants and scalar extension exhibits $C_T(P)^r$ as a split summand of $B_T^{m_r}$. Tensoring with it is exact: on a short exact sequence it takes the image of the same idempotent on a finite direct sum; a local lift of an element in the target image can be projected by that idempotent to a lift in the source image. Thus its terms are flat over $B_T$, and the bounded-above-flat theorem makes $C_T(P)$ K-flat. Derived reduction is consequently its ordinary tensor complex. In every degree the isomorphism is
$$(b\otimes p)\otimes a\longmapsto a\,\operatorname{pr}_n(b)\otimes p,$$
with inverse $a\otimes p\mapsto(1\otimes p)\otimes a$. The balancing equations show these are inverse, and applying $d^r$ in either order sends this element to $a\operatorname{pr}_n(b)\otimes d^rp$. Replacing $a$ by its image modulo $\pi^n$ also commutes with the formula. This proves the first displayed comparison with its specified differential and consecutive quotient maps.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat); finite-summand tensor calculation and K-flat computation of derived change of rings

proof.text: Choose integers $c\le d$ outside which $P^\bullet$ is zero. Apply the completed perfect model completeness lemma with $A=R$, $I=(\pi)$, this bounded complex and either $T$. The Noetherian and maximal-ideal hypotheses were checked in step 1. Its complex $M^\bullet=B_T\otimes_RP^\bullet$ is exactly our displayed complex, with its original scalar differential. Hence $C_T(P)$ is locally derived $(\pi)B_T$-complete: $R\mathcal Hom(B_U[1/b],C_T(P)|_U)=0$ for every slice $U$ and every local section $b$ of $\pi B_T$. By step 1, $(R,(\pi))$ satisfies the adic coefficient datum, and $B_T$ is the coefficient sheaf $\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ of the completeness-equivalence theorem (its auxiliary prime $p$ is any prime $\ne\ell$ and enters none of its conditions). Its implication (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i),(iv) shows that $C_T(P)$ is derived complete in the Roos-triangle sense and that the explicit product-fibre unit of the intrinsic Koszul completion is invertible. This is the completeness required by the specified completed-pullback definition and by the integral-pullback comparison used in step 6; it imposes no finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Tag 099Q (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), bounded perfect scalar model; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.6.11 reverse-direction local model

proof.text: Set $D_{T,n}=(A_n)_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{P^\bullet}_T$, restricted along $\operatorname{pr}_n$. Its quotient cone is $b\otimes p\mapsto\operatorname{pr}_n(b)\otimes p$ from $C_T(P)$. The $R$-linear splitting $i_r,s_r$ of step 2, tensored with $B_T$ and each $(A_n)_T$, makes the degree-$r$ cone a compatible split retract of the $m_r$-fold coefficient cone, degreewise only. By the finite-perfect coefficient-limit theorem, $C_T(P)$ with the quotient maps is the ordinary limit of the complex tower. In each degree $r$ the transition $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}D^r_{T,n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_nD^r_{T,n}$ is $q_{n+1,n}\otimes1$, epi by right exactness of tensor. Hence the epimorphic-tower theorem makes $1-s:\prod_nD^r_{T,n}\to\prod_nD^r_{T,n}$ surjective with kernel the limit, which the coefficient-limit theorem identifies with $C_T(P)^r$ and its quotient maps. Let $\mathsf C(D)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$, with degree-$k$ part $\prod_nD^k\oplus\prod_nD^{k-1}$, and let $b:C_T(P)\to\mathsf C(D)$ have product component the quotient maps and zero shifted component. It is a chain map, since $1-s$ kills the quotient family, and degreewise injective. Its cokernel is identified, through $1-s$ on the first summand, with $\prod_nD^k\oplus\prod_nD^{k-1}$ and differential $(z,y)\mapsto(dz,\pm z-dy)$: the shifted cone of an identity, which is contractible. By the long exact cohomology sequence $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Pro-etale countable products are exact, so the strict Roos comparison theorem applies; it says that $b$ corresponds under its natural isomorphism $\rho_D:\mathsf C(D)\cong R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{T,n}$ to the canonical derived map induced by the strict augmentation, and that $\rho_D$ commutes with every projection. Thus the canonical map $C_T(P)\to R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{T,n}$ (cone model and K-injective strict model alike) is an isomorphism whose projections are the original quotient maps. Both $b$ and $\rho$ are natural in strict maps of towers.

source.place: Tags 0940 (section-derived-limits) and 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), applied to the finite-projective retracts of the actual coefficient cone

proof.text:
At finite level the canonical constant-module inverse-image isomorphisms give $g^{-1}\underline R_V\cong\underline R_{V'}$, $g^{-1}(A_n)_V\cong(A_n)_{V'}$ and $g^{-1}\underline{P^r}_V\cong\underline{P^r}_{V'}$. They preserve constant scalar sections and are natural in $R$-linear maps. Combine them with the inverse-image tensor comparison, then cancel extension along the constant-ring isomorphism. This gives
$$g_n^*D_{V,n}\cong D_{V',n}.$$
On a tensor of constant sections the map is $a\otimes p\mapsto a\otimes p$. On its image under a differential both composites are $a\otimes d^rp$, and under a quotient transition both are $q_{n+1,n}(a)\otimes p$. The tensor comparisons are sheaf maps determined locally by pure tensors, so these equalities prove compatibility on the whole sheaves. Finite-level pullback is exact, hence this is also its derived comparison. It is an isomorphism of the strict towers of complexes, rather than a collection of unrelated derived isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); sites.tex Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf), with canonical constant-section maps

proof.text:
Use $C_V(P)$ itself as the K-flat representative from step 2. By the specified strict reduction-tower pullback, step 5 gives
$$Lg^*C_V(P)\cong R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_nD_{V',n}.$$
The inverse of the comparison in step 4 for $T=V'$ gives the asserted isomorphism with $C_{V'}(P)$, and identifies every projection with its ordinary quotient map. By step 3, $C_V(P)$ is derived complete in the Roos-triangle sense, so the integral-pullback comparison theorem gives a natural isomorphism $Lg^*C_V(P)\cong Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}C_V(P)$ with the strict-tower completed pullback, under which the defining projections of the two derived limits correspond. This is the asserted equivalence of the two pullbacks on this complete object. For a chain map $f:P\to Q$, every displayed reduction map commutes with $1\otimes f$ because both composites send $(b\otimes p)\otimes a$ to $a\operatorname{pr}_n(b)\otimes f(p)$. The ordinary limit cone comparison is natural by its universal property, and the strict derived-limit functor preserves this square. Thus the isomorphisms are natural in chain maps, independently of the auxiliary splittings, which were used only to establish invertibility.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5), interpreted via the specified strict quotient tower; agent assembly and chain-map calculation

proof.text:
The constant-sheaf functor on $R$-modules is additive and exact by the constant-module section-properties theorem. The completed-constant reduction theorem says that $B_T$ is flat over $\underline R_T$, so $M\mapsto B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline M_T$ is additive and exact. Apply exact-functor preservation of complex cohomology to $P^\bullet$. Its comparison is induced by preservation of cycles and boundaries, so for every $j$ it is the canonical natural isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^j(C_T(P))\cong B_T\otimes_{\underline R_T}\underline{H^j(P^\bullet)}_T.$$
This uses flatness over the constant scalar ring; it makes no assertion about flatness of the coefficient map associated with $g$.

For any $R$-module $N$, use the constant-module inverse-image isomorphism and the inverse-image tensor isomorphism to write the ordinary ringed pullback as
$$B_{V'}\otimes_{g^{-1}B_V}\bigl(g^{-1}B_V\otimes_{\underline R_{V'}}\underline N_{V'}\bigr).$$
The projection-induced map $g^\sharp:g^{-1}B_V\to B_{V'}$ agrees on $\underline R_{V'}$ with the target constant-scalar map: composing with every finite projection sends $r$ to its class modulo $\pi^n$ on both sides. The limit universal property proves the equality. Hence the balanced map $b'\otimes(b\otimes n)\mapsto b'g^\sharp(b)\otimes n$ is well defined. Its inverse is $b'\otimes n\mapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes n)$. One composite is the identity by the unit equation, and the other by the balancing equation $b'g^\sharp(b)\otimes(1\otimes n)=b'\otimes(b\otimes n)$. These maps commute with restrictions and are natural in $N$, so they define the asserted canonical isomorphism of module sheaves. Take $N=H^j(P^\bullet)$ and use step 7.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); elementary balanced-tensor cancellation along the projection-induced coefficient map

proof.text: If $j\notin[a,b]$, step 7 identifies the assumed zero sheaf $\mathcal H^j(C_V(P))$ with $B_V\otimes\underline{H^j(P)}_V$. Ordinary ringed pullback sends the zero sheaf to zero, since inverse image and tensor send zero to zero. Step 8 identifies that pullback with $B_{V'}\otimes\underline{H^j(P)}_{V'}$, and step 7 identifies the latter with $\mathcal H^j(C_{V'}(P))$. Therefore the latter vanishes. This argument applies to each $j$ outside the given cohomological interval, irrespective of the degrees in which the chosen representative $P^\bullet$ is supported.
